name: QA gate severity ladder: tests.run-error is medium, so a completely dead test runner reports require_approval instead of block
description:
Finding from the QA shift of 2026-11-24 (evidence: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", extra_args=["--version"])` → exit 1, 0.0s — the pytest executable does not exist in the runtime).

## Problem
`qa_review_changes`, `qa_run_tests` and `qa_coverage` all report `tests.run-error` / `coverage.unavailable` at **medium** severity. Under the current policy (`block_above: high`, `approval_above: medium`, `block_on_failures: true`, `fail_closed: false`) that gives a permanent ceiling of **require_approval**:

- There is no suite that can execute at all (pytest binary missing; node/npm missing for the client JS suite).
- `block_on_failures: true` never triggers, because a crashed command is not counted as a "failure" — the counters are all zero.
- Therefore the QA gate can never escalate to `block` on a repository where literally nothing is verifiable. `require_approval` reads as "medium, fix the tests", which understates an environment where the runner does not exist.

This directly contradicts the QA mandate rule 4: "A missing suite is a finding. 'There is nothing to run' is a HIGH environment finding, not a pass."

## What to do (either one, deliberately)
A. Code fix (preferred): classify `tests.run-error` as **high** when `passed=0 and failed=0 and errors=0 and seconds < 1` — i.e. the command never produced a verdict — so the gate returns `block`. Same for `coverage.unavailable` when `min_coverage > 0` and no report exists.
B. Dated policy change approved by the user: set `fail_closed: true` in `qa_policy` (only the user may waive/approve this).

## Acceptance criteria
- With the runner still broken, `qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` returns `decision: block`, `highest_severity: high`, and a finding id naming the environment cause.
- With a working runner and green tests, the same call returns `allow` — the escalation must not fire on a healthy run (guard: at least one test must have been collected).
- Evidence command: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", extra_args=["--version"])` (currently exit 1, must eventually be exit 0).

## Out of scope
Do not add tests here — that is `b19676fe-d0e8-4a1c-baa2-7863287da1b9` (runner) and `91411767-7eed-4040-b4b7-e66d1e71c014` (node). This card is only the severity/verdict ladder.

Do not add tests here — that is `b19676fe-d0e8-4a1c-baa2-7863287da1b9` (runner) and `91411767-7eed-4040-b4b7-e66d1e71c014` (node). This card is only the severity/verdict ladder.

New evidence for this card (QA shift 2026-11-24, turn 4) — the severity asymmetry is now proven with two data points on the *same* root cause class (a runner that cannot start):

| suite | result | severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm` (no binary in PATH) | `decision: block`, `blocked: True` | **high** `tests.no-runner` |
| `pytest` (binary exits 1 in 0.0s, e.g. `--version`) | `decision: require_approval` | **medium** `tests.run-error` |

Both mean "0 tests can execute", so the gate should not rank them differently. Only the npm branch can ever reach `block`; the Python branch — the one that gates `api/` — is capped at `require_approval` and therefore cannot stop a merge on its own.

Refined acceptance criteria:
1. A runner that fails to start (any suite) must emit a HIGH finding, so `qa_run_tests` returns `block`. `tests.no-runner` already does this; `tests.run-error` does not.
2. Either classify `run-error` with all-zero counters as `no-runner`, or set `fail_closed: true` via a dated, user-approved policy change — not by editing thresholds in the report.
3. Re-verification command: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", extra_args=["--version"])` must return `block` (it currently returns `require_approval`).

[qa shift 2026-11-25T12:xxZ — the ladder asymmetry is now measured, not inferred]

Same dead runtime, two different verdicts, one hour apart:

| command | tool finding | severity | decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", extra_args=["--version"])` | `tests.run-error` (`pytest: exited with code 1`, **0.0 s**) | medium | **require_approval** |
| `qa_run_tests(suite="npm", paths=["tests/company-active-project.test.mjs"])` | `tests.no-runner` (`npm: npm not found in PATH`) | high | **block** |

So: a suite whose runner does not exist is **blocked** when the gate notices at *availability* time and only `require_approval` when it notices at *execution* time — although both mean "zero tests executed". `qa_plan` even reports pytest as `available: True`, so the availability check cannot be the discriminator either.

Acceptance unchanged: any run that executes zero tests because the runner is missing / not importable must be `high` → `block`, reported with the same rule id family as `tests.no-runner`. Re-verify with exactly the two commands above — expected result is `block` for **both**.
